anomalies.observed: On sheet 1, 'Water Temperature Sensor', the Atlas EZO-RTD module M6 has its RX/SDA pin tied to global label NET0097, while its TX/SCL pin is on NET0034 (the main I2C SCL net). NET0097 is not the main I2C SDA net: the ESP32-C6 IO4/I2C_SDA pin, the I2C pull-up resistors (R20/R26/R23), the LiDAR header H7, and the ADM3260 primary-side SDA1 pins all carry NET0067, and the isolated secondary SDA carries NET0087. Thus M6's SDA line sits on a third, otherwise-unused net.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification §4.1, 'M4 (EZO-RTD) — directly, unisolated' on the main I2C bus, so the RTD's SDA must share the main I2C_SDA net (NET0067) together with its SCL (NET0034), exactly as the pH/EC isolator primary sides and the environmental headers do.

evidence.quote: Sheet 1, 'Water Temperature Sensor': M6 ATLAS_EZO_RTD, RX/SDA -> NET0097, TX/SCL -> NET0034; compare SoC M3A IO4/I2C_SDA -> NET0067 and LiDAR H7 SDA -> NET0067
§4.1 Main (non-isolated) I2C bus ... This bus fans out to: M4 (EZO-RTD) — directly, unisolated.

anomalies.impact: The EZO-RTD (PT-1000 water temperature) SDA line is left floating on a net that no other device or pull-up drives, so the sensor cannot acknowledge or be addressed on the I2C bus. Water-temperature reading (and therefore VPD computation and RTD-based dosing compensation) will fail, while pH/EC and the rest of the bus still work.

parsed.summary: Most of the drawing matches the intended r2 design (buck/LDO rails, 52k3/10k feedback for 5 V, 2.2 k I2C pull-ups, 110 mΩ current-sense pairs, isolated pH/EC channels with a shared PDIS, and the documented firmware-vs-schematic pin differences). The one deviation the drawing supports is on the non-isolated temperature sensor: M6's RX/SDA is labelled NET0097 instead of the main I2C_SDA net (NET0067), leaving the EZO-RTD off the I2C bus.
